hinglish.title: Operating System 03 | Process Synchronization & Semaphores | CS & IT | GATE 2025 Crash Course
covers: critical section problem & requirements (mutual exclusion, progress, bounded waiting)
software solutions: turn variable, flag variable, Peterson's solution (framed as a combination/improvisation of the two)
GATE-style semaphore value / numerical questions (worked live, e.g. minimum-value trace at 1:25:00)
mutex (binary semaphore used for mutual exclusion, discussed in reader-writer context)
classical problems of synchronization (labelled explicitly at 1:35:09 — producer-consumer, readers-writers, dining philosophers)
hinglish.why: A single 116-minute GATE-crash-course lecture that, unusually for this topic, is NOT split into short fragments — it chains flag/turn variables into Peterson's solution, semaphores, GATE-style value numericals, and the classical problems in one continuous session. Comment timestamps (37:55, 50:14, 1:25:00, 1:35:09) independently confirm this breadth. One viewer calls it 'the best video of OS, I don't know why its underrated'; engagement (1,102 likes / 31 comments on ~89K views) is modest next to Gate Smashers' shorts, which is expected for a single long lecture vs. many short high-replay clips, but sentiment is uniformly positive with zero accuracy complaints found.

50:14 Peterson's Solution... combination of improvisations of both the previous ones

coverage_gaps: Hinglish: the two final picks do not clearly cover monitors (no strong dedicated Hinglish monitors video was found from a top channel — searches returned only unrelated 'display monitor' results) or the swap instruction (only low-view, non-top-channel videos exist for swap specifically; test-and-set is covered by the L-3.6 pick but swap is not). English: the three final picks (critical section, semaphores, dining philosophers) leave out software/hardware solution algorithms (lock variable, strict alternation, Peterson's — see runner-up gYCiTtgGR5Q, an excellent Peterson's Solution video cut only to respect the 3-video cap), test-and-set/swap hardware instructions (Neso's 'Test and Set Lock' was disqualified for disabled captions), two of the three classical problems (producer-consumer/Bounded Buffer and readers-writers — both exist as strong Neso Academy runners-up), and monitors as a distinctly named concept (Neso's 'Monitors', lowest-viewed in its series, listed as runner-up). Students needing full coverage in English should supplement with Neso Academy's Peterson's Solution, Test and Set Lock (no captions — watch without relying on subtitles), Bounded Buffer Problem, Readers Writers Problem, and Monitors videos, all from the same well-reviewed playlist.
